name: Acid House
summary: Natural-wine-and-brunch spot off Garosu-gil, pairing sourdough and beet rigatoni with a curated wine list.
description: Acid House sits just off Garosu-gil, blending an all-day brunch menu with a natural wine bar identity — sourdough and Danish rye bread with whipped butter, a beet rigatoni and a lemon-basil pasta anchor the food side. Nearly 50 Google reviews average 4.9/5, an unusually high mark, and Kakao reviewers echo the praise. It's a relaxed, design-forward room that works for a daytime brunch stop or an evening wine-and-small-plates session.
highlights: Sourdough & Danish rye with whipped butter
tips: Good for a mid-afternoon brunch that overlaps into wine hour.
It's a 7-minute walk from Sinsa Station, right off Garosu-gil.

It's a two-minute walk from Naebang Station and a genuinely local neighborhood pick rather than a tourist burger stop — handy for a relaxed lunch near Seorae Village or the Express Bus Terminal.

name: Baguetine
summary: European-style artisan bread bakery in Bangbae — plain and walnut-cranberry campagne, fresh from the morning bake.
description: Baguetine is a European-style artisan bakery in Bangbae focused entirely on naturally leavened bread — plain campagne, a walnut-and-cranberry version, and small walnut-blueberry baguette pieces to sample. It's not a sit-down restaurant, more a grab-and-go bakery stop, but a good addition to a morning walk if you want proper crusty bread rather than the sweet pastries most Korean bakeries lean toward. Both Kakao (4.7) and Google (4.6) reviewers rate it well.
tips: It's a bakery, not a sit-down restaurant — good for a breakfast grab before heading out.
Opens early (08:30) — useful for an early-departure day.

name: Baje
summary: Bangbae's fresh-pasta bar — carbonara tagliolini and a white-ragu pappardelle at neighborhood-friendly prices.

A saffron arancini starter and a melanzane (eggplant) dish round out the small plates. Both Kakao (4.4/74) and Google (4.9/15) reviewers rate it highly, and the price point sits comfortably in value territory for the quality of fresh pasta on offer.

name: Balwoo Gongyang
summary: Buddhist temple-food courses opposite Jogyesa — calm, vegan, seasonal and gentle on the stomach.
description: Run by the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, Balwoo Gongyang serves temple cuisine: no meat, fish, garlic or onion, relying instead on mountain greens, fermented jang and seasonal produce. Courses range from a weekday-lunch Seon-sik set to the pre-booked Hui-sik feast. The fifth-floor rooms overlook Jogyesa Temple and feel serene after Insadong's crowds. It held a Michelin star for several years but is not listed among the 2026 starred restaurants.
tips: Weekday lunch Seon-sik is the best value; Hui-sik (₩120,000) needs advance booking.
Naver reviewers bring parents for a healthy, mild meal.
Closed Sundays and 24–26 Sep (Chuseok).
Anguk Station Exit 6, ~5 minutes; combine with Insadong and Jogyesa.

reviews.text: Many praise the gourmet vegan temple food, presentation and service; a minority found some dishes bland or cold.

name: Bao Seoul Seongsu
summary: Taiwanese gua bao and beef noodle soup on Seongsu’s Yeonmujang-gil — a Taipei-street feel in a sleek red room.
description: Bao Seoul brings Taipei street food to Seongsu’s main food lane: pillowy gua bao stuffed with braised pork, lamb, prawn or chicken katsu, plus Taiwanese beef noodle soup, beef-tripe noodles and cold peanut noodles. Naver reviewers say it tastes like being back in Taiwan and rate the room highly. It is a known queue spot among young Seoulites but rarely on foreign visitors’ lists. Combine it with Seongsu’s flagship stores and pop-ups.

Arrive just before 17:00 or on a weekday to skip the usual queue.

name: Bicena
summary: Michelin-star Korean tasting menus on the 81st floor of Lotte World Tower — the most dramatic dining view in Seoul.
description: Bicena sits on the 81st floor of Lotte World Tower, Korea's tallest building, with floor-to-ceiling views over the Han River and Jamsil. The cooking is refined Korean with a Gyeongsang-do accent: house-dry-aged hanwoo sirloin, pork belly and seasonal banchan served on beautiful ceramics. It holds one Michelin star in 2026. Combine it with Seoul Sky or the Lotte World Mall below for a futuristic Jamsil day.

summary: Seafood-forward pasta bar near the Express Bus Terminal, big on burrata pizza and a four-mushroom risotto.
description: Bistro Nu is a warm, low-lit pasta-and-pizza bar a short walk from the Express Bus Terminal, best known for its seafood pasta and a burrata-topped Margherita. The four-mushroom risotto and a wild rocket-and-prosciutto pizza round out a compact, well-loved menu, and corkage is free if you want to bring your own bottle. It's an easy, close-to-home option if you're staying near Seocho or Banpo and want a relaxed Italian dinner without a big production.

summary: Warm, regional Italian cooking from a chef-owner in a small Hannam dining room — one of Seoul's best-loved trattorias.
description: Borgo Hannam is a small, chef-driven trattoria that mixes regional Italian dishes with genuine warmth — reviewers consistently call out owner Antonio's hospitality alongside the sea bream crudo, fried zucchini flowers and black-truffle pizza. It is intimate rather than flashy, with an unmarked entrance typical of Hannam's quieter dining scene. Because it is small, book ahead for a group of five and expect a leisurely, conversation-friendly pace rather than a quick turnover. It suits the parents' taste for comfort and quality over spectacle.

name: Born & Bred
summary: Hanwoo beef omakase from a Majang-dong butcher family: four floors, staff-grilled cuts, private rooms
description: Born & Bred grew out of a hanwoo wholesaler that has traded beef in the Majang-dong meat market since 1978, and it claims Korea's first hanwoo omakase. The new building has a different concept on each floor. The basement Speakeasy serves the full omakase at one 19:00 seating, the 2F hall has à la carte cuts and a casual tasting menu, and 3F has private rooms serving a shorter 13–14-course menu. Staff grill every cut at the table and explain it. The room is polished, with marble counters, copper grills and a butcher case by the door. It is listed in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide and appeared on Asia's 50 Best Restaurants' extended 51–100 list in 2024.
highlights: 2F casual tasting menu with yukhoe (beef tartare) and a mixed beef platter
Brisket hot-pot rice with soybean-paste soup

The 2F hall is the cheaper way in: a 200 g hanwoo platter is ₩100,000 and staff still grill it for you.
Majang Station (Line 5) Exit 3 is a 4-minute walk. You pass the huge Majang meat market on the way.
Closed Tuesdays. The break is 15:00–18:00 and last order is 21:15. Corkage is free for one bottle per person.

summary: Gwangjang Market's famous beef-tartare house: silky yukhoe with pear and egg yolk, and cheap yukhoe bibimbap.
description: Buchon Yukhoe sits in the yukhoe alley of Gwangjang Market and has become one of the market's best-known restaurants. Fresh beef is hand-sliced and dressed with sesame oil and pear, crowned with egg yolk; yukhoe bibimbap is the budget way in. It has appeared in the MICHELIN Guide Seoul and is now hugely popular with foreign visitors. A proper indoor restaurant, it is more comfortable for parents than the market's stall benches.

name: Byeokje Galbi (Bangi flagship)
summary: Seoul's blue-chip hanwoo galbi house: top-grade marbled short rib and ribeye, plus classic Pyongyang naengmyeon
description: Byeokje Galbi has served hanwoo short ribs since 1986, and Korean families book the Bangi-dong flagship near Olympic Park for big celebrations. It buys only top-grade cattle (BMS No. 9) at auction, and in-house butchers cut the beef. The signatures are the 'Seolhwa' diamond-cut saeng-galbi (short rib) and kkot-deungsim (ribeye), grilled for you over charcoal. There is also a serious Pyongyang-style naengmyeon and hanwoo soups for lighter eaters. Staff are formal, the dining rooms are hushed, and upstairs rooms suit a family of five. VisitKorea notes its recognition in the MICHELIN Guide Seoul 2023.

name: Daedo Sikdang (Wangsimni main)
summary: Hanwoo sirloin on cast-iron since 1964 — Seoul's classic beef house, finished with legendary kkakdugi fried rice.
description: Daedo Sikdang has been grilling thick-cut hanwoo sirloin on heavy iron plates in Wangsimni since 1964, and the main branch is still where Seoulites take their parents for a beef night. The menu is short: sirloin, a few special cuts, and kkakdugi (radish kimchi) fried rice made in the beef fat at the end. The main store has been refreshed and expanded into annex buildings, and Naver reviewers mention good ventilation and a spacious room. Prices are high but well below Cheongdam steak houses for comparable hanwoo.

reviews.text: Travellers compare it favourably with famous steakhouses: top-quality cuts and very high-quality beef at prices far below New York steak houses.

Returning diners say the renovated main store and new annex buildings feel clean and pleasant, and the meat is as good as ever.

summary: One of Seoul's 'big four' Pyongyang naengmyeon houses — slushy-cold broth, thick buckwheat noodles and mung-bean jeon.
description: Eulmildae in Yeomni-dong is counted by Korean noodle fans among Seoul's four great Pyongyang naengmyeon houses. tips: Order like a regular: 'georaeng' = broth without the ice slush, 'yang manhi' = extra noodles.

summary: Michelin Bib pork BBQ in Yaksu: thick YBD pork belly grilled by staff, wrapped in grilled basil — worth the famous queue.
description: Gold Pig is often named among Seoul's top three pork houses and holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand. tips: No bookings: register on the CatchTable on-site waitlist from about 10:00; a Sept 2026 reviewer got #25 at 10:00 and was seated ~11:45.

reviews.text: Registered on the CatchTable waitlist around 10:00, got number 25 and was seated 15 minutes after opening; staff grilled everything and the grilled-basil wrap was memorable (Sept 2026).

Food writers describe staff fully cleaning the grill and extractor between parties and serving premium YBD pork cuts.

description: Gigas occupies a bright, pale-wood room on the third floor of Piknic, the art space on Namsan’s lower slope near Hoehyeon. Chef Jung Hawan builds seasonal Mediterranean tasting menus around vegetables and herbs from his family farm about 40 km away, adding seafood and a little meat. description: Hadongkwan has served one dish, gomtang, since 1939: a clear, deeply savoury beef broth with brisket (and tripe if you like) over rice, served in brass bowls. You pay first, choose your size, add scallions and the Seoul-style kkakdugi, and eat quickly among office workers. It opens at 07:00, making it one of the best early breakfasts in central Seoul. It appears in the MICHELIN Guide Seoul 2026.
tips: Go for breakfast (07:00–09:00) to avoid the lunch rush and catch the freshest pot.

Regulars add lots of scallion and skip pepper at first to taste the broth.

reviews.text: Came at 08:00 on a weekday for a hangover breakfast — quiet, and the basic gomtang was clean and comforting (Aug 2026).

description: Haidilao is the Chinese hot-pot chain known for over-the-top hospitality, and its Seocho branch sits one minute from Sinnonhyeon Station in the Gangnam Station district. Split pots let a family combine mild tomato or mushroom broth with fiery mala, and there is a large DIY sauce bar. Staff often speak Chinese and some English, and TripAdvisor reviewers highlight fast service. It is open 10:00–07:00 daily, useful for late dinners.
highlights: Lu rou fan and youtiao sides
tips: Queues are long at dinner — a Naver diner waited 75 minutes from 17:30; weekday 11:00 is almost walk-in.
Tables have a 90-minute limit at busy times.

reviews.text: Reviewers highlight attentive Haidilao-style hospitality, fast service and customisable spicy broths.

summary: The original Dongdaemun dakhanmari since 1978 — a whole chicken simmered at your table, then noodles in the broth.
description: Dakhanmari ('one whole chicken') was born in the alleys of Dongdaemun, and this three-storey restaurant claims the original recipe from 1978. A whole chicken arrives in a basin of broth with potatoes and rice cakes, simmering on a burner at your table; you dip pieces in a mix of chilli paste, soy, vinegar and mustard. Finish by adding kalguksu noodles to the rich broth. It is loud, fast, cheap and open until 1 am — perfect after Dongdaemun shopping.

Small room — a group of five may be split; go before 12:00 or after 14:00.

description: Mongtan made its name with u-dae-galbi: thick bone-in beef short ribs seared over burning rice straw (jjipbul) downstairs, then finished at your table by staff. The building is a renovated older house near the War Memorial, with a bustling open grill room on the ground floor. Expect a smoky, fragrant, lively room rather than a quiet one. Queues are legendary, but the payoff is some of the most talked-about beef in the city.

description: Myeongdong Kyoja has served the same short menu — kalguksu, mandu, bibim-guksu and summer kongguksu — since 1966, and Naver shows over 40,000 visitor reviews. name: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market
summary: Seoul's giant live-seafood market: pick crab, fish and shellfish from the tanks, then eat it sliced or steamed upstairs.
description: Noryangjin is Seoul's main wholesale seafood market, now housed in a modern multi-level building beside Noryangjin Station. The ground floor is a sea of glowing tanks – king crab, snow crab, flounder, abalone, scallops, sea squirt – with vendors calling out prices. You buy by weight downstairs, the vendor cleans and slices it, and you carry it up to one of the 2nd-floor 'sangcharim' restaurants, which charge a per-person table fee and extra for steaming or for a spicy fish stew (maeuntang) made from the leftover frames. It is loud, wet-floored and brilliantly theatrical; the upstairs rooms are plain and functional rather than pretty.
highlights: Steamed king crab or snow crab (daege), with crab-butter fried rice made in the shell
Hoe (sliced raw fish) platter – flounder (gwang-eo) and rockfish (ureok)
Maeuntang – spicy stew made from the fish frames
Live scallops, abalone and prawns grilled or steamed upstairs
tips: Prices change daily and are per kg – check the TPirates (인어교주해적단) app for the day's going rate, agree the weight and total before anyone starts cleaning, and don't be shy to compare two or three stalls.
Upstairs restaurants charge a table-setting fee per person (e.g. Chungnam Sikdang lists ₩5,000 pp; maeuntang ₩10,000–15,000) plus steaming fees – ask the fee before sitting down.
Floors are wet and fishy downstairs; wear closed shoes. The building has parking and elevators, and upstairs restaurants take groups of 5 easily.
From home: Line 9 express from Express Bus Terminal reaches Noryangjin in about 10 minutes; use Line 9 Exit 7 or Line 1 Exit 9 and follow signs.

tripadvisor.rank: #65 of 1,622 things to do in Seoul

reviews.text: Travellers call it a seafood lover's paradise: choose live seafood downstairs and have it prepared upstairs for an extra fee.
A recurring complaint: upstairs table and cooking fees can add up to more than expected, so bargain and confirm prices first.
Korean visitors most often praise the easy parking, how much there is to see, the huge variety and friendly vendors.

price.note: Seafood priced by weight at daily market rates; plus upstairs table fee (e.g. ₩5,000 pp) and stew/steaming fees

hours.note: Retail floor trades around the clock (most general stalls ~01:30–22:00); auctions closed Sundays. Upstairs restaurant hours vary by restaurant – late morning to late evening is the easy window.

chuseok.note: Official 2026 notice: only the wholesale auction pauses (25–28 Sep); restaurants and retail stalls operate normally through the holiday. Individual stalls may still take a day off.

name: Nostimo
summary: Greek-owned taverna by Naebang Station, minutes from home: feta, dakos, dolmades, pies and dips with pita.
description: Nostimo (“tasty” in Greek) is a small, bright taverna on the second floor of a Seocho-daero building, three minutes from Naebang Station and a short ride from home. The Greek owner and staff greet diners and explain dishes, which range from baked feta with oregano, Greek salad and Cretan dakos to dolmades, fried saganaki with honey and sesame, chicken pie and a trio of dips with pita. Naver regulars love discovering unfamiliar dishes, and it is almost unknown to visitors.

name: Okdongsik
summary: Michelin Bib clear pork gomtang at a tiny wooden counter in Hapjeong — Jirisan black pork, paper-thin slices, kimchi mandu.
description: Okdongsik reinvented dwaeji gukbap as a crystal-clear, gomtang-style broth made only from the legs of Jirisan black pigs. Rice is warmed by repeatedly pouring broth over it (toryeom), and thin slices of pork fan across the top. The room is a minimalist wooden counter with very few seats, so it suits small splits of the group rather than five together. It has held a Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2018 and is still listed in 2026.
tips: Counter-only and tiny — a family of five will be seated in pairs; go off-peak.

reviews.text: Food guides describe an exceptionally clear broth from the ham and foreleg of Jirisan black pigs, subtle yet elegant, with delicately made kimchi dumplings.

Naver reviewers most often praise the taste and the clean, comforting broth.

summary: Michelin-listed Singaporean roast house in Nonhyeon: crackling roast pork, duck and Hainanese chicken rice.
description: Named after Singapore’s latitude, One Degree North roasts Cantonese-style ducks and crispy pork belly in an oven imported from Singapore, hanging them behind a neon-lit window. Signatures are Hainanese chicken rice, roast duck rice and noodles, char siu and chilli-oil wontons. The Michelin Guide Seoul has listed it for several consecutive years. Family sets for two to four make ordering easy, and Naver diners say portions are generous and parents enjoy it.

The 4-person C-Set (₩95,000) plus one extra dish feeds five.

name: Onjium
summary: Royal-court and noble-household recipes reimagined, facing Gyeongbokgung's stone wall — Michelin one star.
description: Onjium is the restaurant of a research institute devoted to Korean heritage food, clothing and architecture. Its team studies Joseon-era court and aristocratic recipe books and turns them into precise seasonal tasting menus. The fourth-floor room is calm and minimal, looking across to the western wall of Gyeongbokgung Palace. It holds one Michelin star in 2026 and is one of Seoul's hardest reservations.
tips: Lunch ₩200,000 vs dinner ₩300,000; Korean-liquor pairing is cheaper than wine (Naver menu, 2026).
Book the moment slots open; tables for five are rare, so ask early.
Closed Sundays, Mondays and 24–26 Sep (Chuseok).

summary: Flower-filled brunch restaurant inside a Sinsa hotel — salmon eggs Benedict and a pork-and-perilla pasta.
description: Only Go & Co occupies the ground floor of the Sunshine Hotel on Dosan-daero, styled with flowers and soft light for a brunch crowd that skews toward celebrations and dates. The menu fuses Korean ingredients into Western brunch and pasta — a jowl-and-perilla-leaf pasta, salmon eggs Benedict, a short-rib galbi pie and a water-parsley croissant. With 566 Google reviews at 4.8/5, it's one of the most popular brunch spots between Sinsa and Apgujeong, so reservations matter.

Go for brunch (opens 09:30) to catch the best light in the flower-filled room.

name: Oreno Ramen (Main)
summary: Michelin Bib Gourmand ramen in Hapjeong: creamy chicken paitan broth, blended to a froth, for about ₩13,000.
description: Oreno Ramen’s original Hapjeong shop has been a Michelin Bib Gourmand every year since 2019, according to Naver diners, and it is the city’s best-known tori paitan (chicken-bone) ramen. The broth is blitzed until frothy and served with chicken chashu, wood-ear mushrooms and a soft egg; the spicy kara paitan is the local favourite. Ordering is by kiosk and seating is mostly a counter plus small tables. Expect a line at peak meal times, but turnover is quick.
tips: Open through Chuseok with regular 11:00–22:00 hours on 24–26 Sep (Naver listing) — rare for a Hongdae-area favourite.
No break time: go around 14:30–16:30 on a weekday to skip the queue, as Naver diners recommend.
Choose coriander or kimchi at the kiosk; seats are mostly counter, so a group of five may be split.

reviews.text: A diner notes it has been a Michelin Bib Gourmand for eight straight years since 2019, explaining the long queues outside.

Travel guides describe a clean, less greasy chicken broth, with refills available on noodles, rice and broth.

summary: Hannam's fresh-pasta specialist — hand-cut tajarin, ravioli and beef carpaccio in a snug osteria-style room.

summary: Pierre Gagnaire’s French restaurant on Lotte Hotel’s 35th floor: Murano chandeliers, gold trim and a sweep over Seoul.
description: Opened in 2008 atop the Lotte Hotel’s New Wing, this is the three-Michelin-star Parisian chef’s Seoul outpost, listed in the current Michelin Guide Seoul selection. The dining room is classic French luxury — Murano chandeliers, gold trim, orange velvet chairs — with windows over downtown and Namsan. Courses are multi-part and playful in Gagnaire’s style, using mostly local ingredients. TripAdvisor opinions are mixed on value, but Naver diners consistently praise the view, service and set-piece dishes.
tips: Lunch Déjeuner (₩180,000) gives the view at the lowest price; dinner courses are ₩280,000–320,000.

summary: Michelin Bib Pyongyang naengmyeon near Namsangol Hanok Village — clear, peppery broth and handmade mandu.
description: Pildong Myeonok belongs to the Uijeongbu school of Pyongyang cold noodles: a very clear, lightly peppery broth topped with chilli flakes and scallion, and firm buckwheat noodles. name: Pro Soy Crab (Sinsa main branch)
summary: Seoul's best-known soy-marinated raw crab house since 1980 – roe-packed female blue crab, 3 min from Sinsa Station.
description: Pro Soy Crab has served ganjang gejang – raw female blue crab cured in soy – on the same Sinsa corner since 1980, and now fills a multi-storey building with around 300 seats. The crab arrives cold and glossy, the shell full of orange roe; you squeeze the sweet flesh onto rice, then mix rice into the shell with the soy and wrap it in laver. The spicy yangnyeom version is sticky, sweet and garlicky, and the crab-roe bibimbap is a gentler option for anyone wary of raw seafood. It is busy, efficient and very used to international guests.
highlights: Ganjang gejang – soy-marinated female blue crab (2 crabs per order)
tips: For 5 people, one large ganjang + one large yangnyeom order plus a roe bibimbap covers a tasting; rice is extra (a reviewer paid ₩1,000 a bowl) and refills are expected.
Prices are high and in-store menus may not match Naver's listing (one July 2026 reviewer paid ₩136,000 for the extra-large two-crab order) – ask the price for each size when ordering.
Locals say order the gyeran-jjim (steamed egg) and skip the crab stew; the soy crab is the reason to come.
Exit 4 of Sinsa Station, 150 m then into the Starbucks side street; valet parking ₩4,000. Group seating is available on several floors.

reviews.text: An April 2026 visitor found the crab fresh with no fishy smell, and singled out the soft, silky steamed egg on the side.
Pricey, but reviewers say it is worth the visit and they did not regret spending the money.
Korean regulars say it is less salty than other gejang houses, with sweet, firm crab; several note it is now full of foreign visitors.
Critical locals complain the paper menu shows no prices and that valet parking is charged even though the restaurant owns the building.

summary: A British-leaning organic bakery-brunch spot in Cheongdam, serving all-day brunch until 5pm.
description: Queens Park Cheongdam is a European-style bakery and brunch restaurant known for its own bread and pastries, plus an all-day brunch menu that runs until 5pm — a relaxed, low-effort option that suits a slow morning or long lunch. The Cheongdam branch draws a design-conscious local crowd, with a bright, photogenic dining room. It's a comfortable pick after a Chuseok morning walk or before an afternoon in Apgujeong Rodeo, without needing a dinner-level reservation push.

name: Samarkand
summary: Uzbek canteen in Dongdaemun’s Central Asian quarter since 2003: tandoor shashlik, plov, lagman and manti.
description: Behind Dongdaemun History & Culture Park lies a small Central Asian quarter, and Samarkand has served Uzbek home cooking there since 2003, according to Visit Seoul. Lamb shashlik is grilled over fire, plov rice is glossy with meat stock, and hand-pulled lagman, manti dumplings, shurpa and borscht fill the menu. Naver diners say the interior feels like being in Uzbekistan and flavours are mild enough for anyone. Almost no Western tourists find it.
tips: Open through Chuseok 09:00–23:00 on 24–27 Sep (Naver).
Closed on alternate Tuesdays — call before going on 29 Sep.

name: Samwon Garden
summary: Apgujeong's big galbi house since 1976: marinated short ribs grilled by staff, beside a landscaped garden
description: Samwon Garden has served marinated galbi (short ribs) in Apgujeong since 1976, and it reopened in 2022 after a full rebuild. The new building has high ceilings and glass walls onto a landscaped garden, which makes the large hall bright and calm even when it is full. Staff grill the beef at the table, from the signature soy-marinated galbi to hanwoo sirloin and special cuts. There is also a long list of dishes for people who don't want meat, such as naengmyeon, galbi-tang and ganjang-gejang (soy-marinated crab). The MICHELIN Guide lists it as a Selected restaurant for 2026, recommended for groups.
highlights: Weekday lunch set with hanwoo bulgogi (₩55,000)
Naengmyeon to finish (a ₩11,000 taster portion is on the menu)
tips: The weekday-only lunch set costs ₩55,000 per person (minimum two people). You choose hanwoo bulgogi, soy crab or barley-dried croaker, with naengmyeon or doenjang stew, which makes it the good-value way in.
Private rooms seat groups. Book one for five on CatchTable, especially for dinner and weekends.
Order a small taster naengmyeon (맛보기 냉면) after the galbi, as Korean regulars do. Parking is easy, and on Naver it is often praised as roomy and clean.
Apgujeong Station (Line 3) Exit 3 is about an 8-minute walk. The break is 14:30–17:30 on weekdays and 14:30–17:00 at weekends.

name: Seongsu Jokbal
summary: One of Seoul's 'top three' jokbal: glossy, chewy trotters in an old-school Seongsu shop locals queue for.
description: Seongsu Jokbal has been braising trotters in the old factory district since the 1980s and is routinely named among Seoul's three best jokbal. The skin is glossy and bouncy, the meat soft, and the fat pleasantly firm. It is a small, plain, busy room just off Seongsu Station — a contrast to the neighbourhood's designer cafés and pop-ups. Many locals simply take it away.
tips: Hidden gem: 4,700+ Naver visitor reviews but few foreign reviews; Seongsu residents' No. 1 pick in local guides.
Queues are long at dinner; a Sept 2026 reviewer walked in within 30 minutes near closing.

summary: Bangbae's most-loved meat house, two minutes from Naebang Station — a Korean Meat Master's garlic-marinated galbi-sal.

tips: Window seats cost an extra ₩30,000 on Fri–Sun lunches per a Naver reviewer — worth it on a clear day.
STAY Fun (₩135,000) is the entry course; pair with Seoul Sky or Lotte World Mall.

description: Soonhee's has fried bindaetteok in Gwangjang Market for about 40 years. description: Summer Lane brings an Australian all-day brunch to a Hannam side street, with yellow awnings, beach murals and pastel tables. The menu covers smashed avocado, croissant French toast, waffle eggs Benedict with bacon or salmon, sausage rolls, lamingtons and pavlova, plus proper flat whites and long blacks. name: Wangbijib Myeongdong Main
summary: Staff-grilled marinated pork and hanwoo in the middle of Myeongdong — the easy, visitor-friendly BBQ after shopping.
description: Wangbijib is a Myeongdong institution for galbi and marinated pork, set on a second floor a few minutes from Myeongdong Station. Staff grill for you, the side dishes are neat, and room-like booths make it calmer than the street outside. It is used to foreign guests, which makes ordering easy, and lunch sets arrive already cooked. It is not a hidden gem, but it is a reliable, comfortable BBQ in the city's busiest shopping district.
tips: At lunch the set meals come pre-grilled — no smoke on your clothes before an afternoon of shopping (Naver review).
Booth-style tables give a quieter meal; good for five.
Myeongdong Station Exit 8 is ~3 minutes away.
Several Wangbijib branches exist in Myeongdong; this is the main store (명동본점).

reviews.text: Described as a true representation of Korean BBQ with impeccable service; some reviewers find it pricier than other BBQ spots but agree the meat is premium.

Sweet charcoal-scented pork galbi, good value right in central Myeongdong — suits all ages and foreign visitors.

name: Wolfgang’s Steakhouse Cheongdam
summary: Korea’s first Wolfgang’s: sizzling dry-aged USDA Prime porterhouse carved tableside in a big, polished Cheongdam room.
description: Founded by a 40-year Peter Luger veteran, Wolfgang’s opened its first Korean branch in Cheongdam, and it remains the city’s benchmark New York–style steakhouse. USDA Prime beef is dry-aged in-house for 22–28 days, broiled and served sizzling in butter, carved at the table. The brick building has plenty of space for groups, and Naver shows over 10,000 visitor reviews praising the steak, service and celebratory feel. TripAdvisor scores are more modest (3.9), with some diners citing price.
highlights: Porterhouse for two or more (1 kg ₩370,000)
tips: The lunch course (₩130,000) is the value way in; book CatchTable early — slots can close early when fully reserved.
A 1 kg porterhouse plus sides comfortably feeds three; add a filet for five.

name: Woo Lae Oak
summary: Since 1946: the benchmark Pyongyang cold noodles in hanwoo broth, plus old-school bulgogi — a Michelin Bib Seoul legend.
description: Woo Lae Oak has served Pyongyang-style naengmyeon in Euljiro since 1946, and many Seoulites still consider it the reference bowl. The broth is simmered from hanwoo shank and seasoned only with salt and soy, so it tastes clean and beefy rather than sweet. Big, bright dining halls over two floors take families easily, and bulgogi grilled at the table makes a classic pairing. It is listed as a Bib Gourmand in the MICHELIN Guide Seoul 2026.
tips: Weekend waits of 1.5–2.5 hours were reported in Aug 2026 — register at the door and explore Gwangjang Market or Cheonggyecheon while you wait.
Weekdays have a 14:00–17:00 break; arrive at 11:30 or just before 17:00.
Closed Mondays and across Chuseok (24–26 Sep).
Valet parking available; Euljiro 4-ga Station Exit 4 is 2 minutes away.

reviews.text: A terrific traditional place for bulgogi and especially Pyongyang cold noodles; service is fast and a bit brusque but friendly. Some find prices high for bulgogi.

name: Woocheon Meat Restaurant
summary: Cheongdam butcher-shop-style hanwoo grill — pick your 1++ cuts from the counter, then have them grilled tableside.
description: Woocheon runs the 정육식당 (butcher-restaurant) format popular across Seoul: a meat counter up front where you choose your 1++ hanwoo cuts, then a dining room where staff grill them tableside. The signature is a mixed grill of premium specialty cuts, backed by a hanwoo doenjang stew, hanwoo yukhoe naengmyeon (cold noodles with raw beef) and a hanwoo-fat fried rice to finish. It's a straightforward, high-quality hanwoo night in Cheongdam without the flashier price tag of some nearby tasting-menu steakhouses.
tips: Order the mixed cuts platter first, then finish with the fried rice cooked in the leftover fat.
Free corkage if you want to bring wine.

reviews.text: Reviewers praise the deep flavor of the 1++ aged hanwoo and the butcher-shop-style transparency on cuts.

summary: Charcoal yakitori omakase in Yeonnam from chef Kim Byoung-mook, the “yakitori king” of Netflix’s Culinary Class Wars.
description: Chef Kim Byoung-mook grills free-range chicken over binchotan and straw along a long open counter, working through thigh, heart, skin and tsukune with a poached egg. The Michelin Guide Seoul lists the restaurant, and his run on Netflix’s Culinary Class Wars made seats harder to get. Naver diners call the omakase juicy and good value for the quality, though one found a recent visit over-salted. There is also a newer Sinsa branch closer to home.

name: Yeongdong Seolleongtang
summary: Milky ox-bone seolleongtang served almost round the clock by Sinsa Station for 30+ years — Gangnam's classic late meal.
description: Yeongdong Seolleongtang has fed Gangnam night owls for decades from a corner near Sinsa Station, three stops from home on Line 3. The menu is essentially one soup — rich, milky ox-bone broth with thin slices of beef and noodles — plus suyuk for sharing, and rice or broth refills are free. It is open around the clock apart from a 15:00–17:00 break, recently renovated, and has its own parking lot.
tips: Season it yourself with salt, scallion and pepper at the table; ask for extra noodles.
Open 24 hours except a 15:00–17:00 break — perfect after a late night in Sinsa or Garosu-gil.

name: Yu Yuan (Four Seasons Seoul)
summary: Michelin-starred Cantonese room at the Four Seasons: carved Peking duck, dim sum lunches and 1920s-Shanghai glamour.
description: Yu Yuan on the Four Seasons’ 11th floor channels 1920s Shanghai with teal walls, brass screens and lamp-lit tables. The Michelin-starred kitchen is Cantonese at heart: Peking duck carved tableside, barbecued char siu, double-boiled soups and a strong dim sum lunch. Naver reviewers praise balanced seasoning and staff who greet every guest; many choose it for anniversaries and parents’ milestones. Private rooms make it easy for a family of five.
tips: Lunch Delights course (₩140,000) is the gentlest entry; dinner courses run ₩280,000–320,000.
Order the Peking duck in advance when booking.

reviews.text: Reviewers recommend the Peking duck and popular lunchtime dim sum, calling it a good place for family gatherings and special events.

description: Zero Complex is a MICHELIN Guide-listed restaurant led by chef Lee Choong-hoo, who draws on his time at Paris's acclaimed Le Chateaubriand for a French tasting-course menu built around seasonal ingredients. The room near Seobinggo is understated and calm, aimed at guests who want serious cooking without excess formality. It is a good pick for a quieter, food-focused evening rather than a big group celebration, and reviewers rate it highly despite modest review volume. Book ahead as seating is limited.

summary: A neighbourhood patbingsu shop in Ichon whose slow-cooked red beans draw Seoulites across the river

name: London Bagel Museum Anguk
summary: Seoul's most famous bagel shop: London-deli interiors, 20+ chewy bagels and queues that need the CatchTable remote waitlist
description: The original London Bagel Museum is a two-storey brick-and-wood space in Bukchon styled like an old London deli, with royal portraits, Union Jacks and baskets of bagels stacked to the ceiling. The chewy bagels start at 3,800원 (plain) and most flavours are 4,700원; the spring-onion cream cheese bagel and the Jambon butter sandwich bagel are the classics. Naver visitors rate it 4.21 with 9,000+ reviews and mostly praise the bread and the photogenic interior. TripAdvisor reviewers love the bagels but warn about long waits.

name: Namusairo Coffee
summary: A long-respected Seoul specialty roaster, pouring monthly single origins in a hanok by Gyeongbokgung
description: Namusairo ('between the trees') is a respected Seoul specialty roaster that moved into a restored hanok with a tiny garden in Naeja-dong, four minutes from Gyeongbokgung Station. Beans rotate monthly and the baristas explain each origin; the espresso and filter coffee are the reason to go, with an amaretto latte and specialty tiramisu for non-purists. TripAdvisor rates it 4.4, and on Naver 'great coffee' is by far the most-voted praise.
highlights: Rain dripping from the hanok eaves
tips: Opens 07:30 — a perfect first stop before Gyeongbokgung gates open.

name: Nudake Tea House Seongsu
summary: Gentle Monster's dessert label in a sculptural Seongsu tea lounge — plates that look like art objects
description: Nudake is the dessert brand of eyewear house Gentle Monster, known for pastries that look like sculptures. Its Seongsu tea house, one of the brand's newest spaces, sits above a gift shop in a vast, gallery-like building on Ttukseom-ro: you browse the ground floor, then climb to a hushed tea lounge. The menu is conceptual — the Peak Small cake, the 155MM, a nine-piece petits fours collection (34,000원) — paired with house teas. Naver visitors (4.71) love the concept and design; several say it is pricey and 'not about value'.
highlights: Tea pairings in the upper lounge

Budget ~25,000–35,000원 per person; share plates across the family.
13 min walk from Seongsu Stn Exit 3; combine with Seoul Forest.

description: On the 3rd–4th floors above Gyeongdong Market, the former 1960s Gyeongdong Theatre was restored as a Starbucks that keeps the stepped auditorium as seating. Naver reviewers note it was picked among the Korea Tourism Organization × Starbucks top-10 special stores, and it sells store-only drinks such as a honey-hotteok latte. TripAdvisor rates it 4.7, and on Naver the interior is by far the most praised feature.
highlights: Gyeongdong Market herb & ginseng alleys below
tips: Enter at Gyeongdong Market Gate 4 (Gwangseong Arcade); 6 min from Jegi-dong Stn Exit 2.
Naver lists it open 08:00–22:00 on 24–26 Sep, but many market stalls close for Chuseok — go 27 Sep or later for the market.
Weekend tiered seats fill up; weekday mornings are easy for 5.
Standard Starbucks prices and app (Siren Order) work here.

name: Starbucks Seoul Wave Art Center
summary: A Starbucks floating on the Han River at Jamwon — wall-to-wall water views, 15 minutes from home by taxi
description: Seoul Wave Art Center is a floating culture complex moored at Jamwon Hangang Park in Seocho-gu, and its Starbucks puts glass walls right on the water, facing the Han River and the northern skyline. It works like any Starbucks (app ordering, coupons), with standard prices. Naver visitors vote 'great view' most, and reviewers praise both daytime and night views; one notes you can walk on to Banpo Bridge for the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain.
tips: Open 07:00–22:00 on 24–27 Sep (posted on Naver) — a reliable open spot on Chuseok day.
Jamwon Stn Exit 3/4 is a 15-min walk; bus 143/345/4318 to 잠원한신아파트 then 5 min, or a short taxi from home.
More window seats were added recently, per Naver reviews.
Check the Banpo Bridge fountain schedule and walk there after sunset.

name: Sulbing Gangnam Station
summary: Korea’s best-known bingsu chain: fluffy milk-snow bingsu to share, open through Chuseok at Gangnam Station
description: Sulbing popularised the fluffy 'snow' milk bingsu, starting with the injeolmi (roasted soybean & rice cake) bingsu, and a single bowl easily serves two or three people. This Gangnam Station branch is upstairs, behind the SPAO building, and is a practical, inexpensive dessert stop near home. Naver visitors vote desserts first and 214 call it good value.
tips: Open 11:30–22:00 on all Chuseok days (posted on Naver).
Order 2 bowls for 5 people.
Gangnam Stn Exit 11 (5 min) — 2 stops from Seocho/Gyodae on Line 2.

name: Suyeon Sanbang
summary: Tea in novelist Lee Tae-jun's 1930s hanok home in Seongbuk-dong — jujube tea and pumpkin bingsu in a secret garden
description: Suyeon Sanbang is the former house of short-story writer Sangheo Lee Tae-jun, who lived here from 1933 to 1946; it is now a tea house in the hills of Seongbuk-dong. Guests sit on the maru or in the small garden with jujube ssanghwa tea (15,500원) or the famous pumpkin bingsu and red-bean porridge. Naver reviewers call it especially atmospheric on rainy days; they also note it is small, the chairs are not built for long stays and prices are high.
highlights: Garden seating by the old house
tips: Closed Mondays and Tuesdays; closes at 17:50 on weekdays, 19:50 on weekends.
No subway nearby: take Line 4 to Hansung Univ. then bus 1111/2112 to the 이태준가옥 stop, or a taxi (~40 min from home).
Small rooms — a group of 5 may be split; weekday early afternoon is calmest.
Pair with Gilsangsa temple (10 min walk) for a quiet half-day.

reviews.text: Reviewers describe a small but charming reformed hanok where you look at the old house's back garden over tea; calm and atmospheric, though not cheap.
A rainy-day visitor loved the mood and the not-too-sweet homemade red beans, but found the chairs uncomfortable for a long stay.

name: Taegeukdang
summary: Seoul’s oldest bakery (1946): retro hall, butter bread and the legendary milk monaka ice cream
description: Taegeukdang has baked in Jangchung-dong since 1946 and is widely called Seoul's oldest surviving bakery; the hall keeps its retro signage and old-Seoul feel. Order the milk monaka ice-cream sandwich (3,300원), butter bread (3,100원) and 'sarada' salad bread, which regulars say first-timers must try. Naver visitors (22,000+ reviews) vote 'bread is delicious' above all; TripAdvisor is more mixed at 3.7 over 55 reviews.
tips: Open every day of Chuseok; 25 Sep closes early at 19:00 (posted on Naver).
Right at Dongguk Univ. Stn Exit 2 (Line 3 direct from Nambu Bus Terminal, no transfer).
Pair with Jangchung-dong jokbal street or the Namsan walk.
Traditional gift boxes (from 22,000원) make easy souvenirs.

summary: A no-kids rooftop café in Songridan-gil with a Lotte World Tower view over soft-serve monaka and iced tea.
description: On the 9th floor of an office building in Jamsil's Songridan-gil, Thirsty Ant is a quiet, adults-oriented rooftop café that frames a close-up view of Lotte World Tower. description: Urban Plant occupies the observation-café building on the south end of Hangang Bridge, so you sit above the water with the river and Nodeul Island around you. summary: A Banpo neighbourhood bakery famous for its pillowy premium milk loaf and house jams — five minutes from Banpo Station
description: Whitelier's original shop sits in the Banpo Shopping Center arcade, reached through the underground passage from Banpo Station (Line 7) and the GOTO Mall. It is known for one thing above all: the premium 'saeng-sikppang' milk loaf (11,000원 full, 6,000원 half), eaten plain or with house jams like strawberry-butter and Earl Grey milk (8,000–9,000원). Use Banpo Stn underground passage exit G14 (~30 m); from home it is about 10 min by taxi or Line 3→7 via Express Bus Terminal.
Buy a loaf plus one jam for a family breakfast — mostly takeaway.

name: 37 Grill & Bar
summary: A 37th-floor whisky and cigar lounge at Conrad Seoul with 180-degree Han River views and 250+ whiskies.
description: 37 Grill & Bar sits on the top floor of Conrad Seoul in Yeouido, combining a classic whisky-and-cigar-lounge feel with 180-degree views over the Han River and city skyline. The whisky list runs past 250 bottles, including rare selections and SMWS bottlings, alongside seasonal signature cocktails, making it a natural fit for parents who enjoy a proper spirits menu in a refined setting. It carries one of the strongest TripAdvisor track records of any bar in this list, with over 250 reviews. Come for the view at golden hour and stay for the whisky.
tips: Book a window table for sunset over the Han River.
Smart-casual dress recommended for this hotel lounge.

summary: Alice in Wonderland speakeasy behind a flower shop; No. 13 in Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026, with theatrical cocktails.
description: You enter Alice through a small flower shop at street level, then take a hidden door down into a dim basement lounge. In 2026 it ranked No. 13 in Asia's 50 Best Bars. Naver marks it as group-friendly with valet parking, so a family table of 5 is realistic if you book.

name: All That Jazz
summary: Korea's oldest jazz club (since 1976), now in a dramatic all-red Itaewon room with live bands every night of the week.
description: All That Jazz opened in Itaewon in 1976 and is the country's oldest active jazz club; in 2023 it moved into a 275 m² second-floor space on Itaewon-ro designed by studio mttb, reached through a red door and a neon-lit corridor. The room is wrapped in red curtains and banquettes, with a long bar and a proper stage for piano, horns and big bands. There are two sets on weeknights (19:00–20:00 and 20:30–23:00) and three on Fridays and Saturdays, the last running until 02:50. The music charge is ₩15,000 per person per set, paid on the night, on top of cocktails, wine and plates.
highlights: Live jazz 364 days a year, with a new line-up nightly
Red, cinematic 2023 interior by mttb, with a long cocktail bar
Fri/Sat three-set nights; bands and quintets in the early set
tips: Cover is ₩15,000 per person per set (two sets = ₩30,000); it is charged on the night, not when you book.
For 5 people incl. parents, book a table in advance on the club's website or Kakao channel and go for the 19:00 or 20:30 set; weeknights are calmer and walk-ins usually work for couples.
Naver reviewers suggest window seats, and eating dinner elsewhere first — drinks are the strength here.
No building parking; valet is reported at the nearby IBK bank branch. Itaewon Stn (Line 6) Exit 3 is about a 6-minute walk.

name: Bar 81 (Signiel Seoul)
summary: Champagne sky bar on the 81st floor of Lotte World Tower: floor-to-ceiling windows over the Han River and all of Seoul.
description: Bar 81 sits inside Signiel Seoul on the 81st floor of Lotte World Tower, Korea's tallest building, so the view out of the full-height windows takes in the Han River bridges on one side and the Jamsil/Gangnam skyline on the other. The room is dark and dramatic, with a double-height ceiling hung with a cloud of glass 'champagne bubbles' and a long marble bar. It is known for one of Asia's largest champagne lists, plus classic and signature cocktails and French-style snack plates (cheese, charcuterie). Forbes Travel Guide named it among the world's best hotel sky bars in 2019. On Friday and Saturday nights a DJ plays, and reviewers report a per-person entrance charge on weekends.
highlights: Window table at sunset, then the lights-on night view (roughly 18:00–20:00 in late September)
Champagne by the glass from a very deep list
Signature cocktails with a cheese or charcuterie plate
Friday–Saturday DJ set 21:30–23:15 (per a Jan 2026 visitor report)
tips: Book a window table in advance (CatchTable or +82-2-3213-1281); a Jan 2026 visitor says window seats are fought over and weekend walk-ins are hard. Online booking slots run 17:00–21:00.

Money flags: a Jan 2026 blog reports a weekend entrance charge of about ₩31,000 per person, and one TripAdvisor reviewer (Oct 2023) says staff asked every member of their group to order. Assume everyone orders at least one drink.
Dress smart casual (no gym wear or flip-flops). The bar has its own smoking room, so the main room stays smoke-free.
Enter at the Signiel lobby entrance at the base of Lotte World Tower (not the Seoul Sky observatory queue) and take the hotel lift up. Pair it with dinner in Lotte World Mall below.

name: Bar Cham
summary: Hanok cocktail bar in Seochon built on Korean spirits and soju; No. 33 in Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026.
description: Bar Cham sits in a renovated hanok (traditional house) in Seochon, with oak beams and hand-built furniture. Staff guide you through traditional Korean spirits (jeontongju) from across the country, and the cocktails are built on soju and local liquors. It placed No. 33 in Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026. The room is calm rather than loud, and it is often cited as one of the most distinctly Korean bars in the city.

summary: Hongdae's 25-year-old jazz club: two live sets nightly a few steps from the stage, for about ₩15,000–20,000 entry.
description: Club Evans, named after pianist Bill Evans, has been the home stage of Korea's young jazz scene near Hongik University since 2001 and runs its own label. There is no barrier between stage and tables, so you sit a few metres from the players. Doors open at 19:00, the first set runs 20:00–20:50 and the second 21:20–22:10, with a different band every night and open jam sessions on Mondays and Tuesdays. Entry is ₩15,000 Sunday–Friday and ₩20,000 on Saturday, plus one drink per person; cocktails and beer are simple and inexpensive.

summary: Legendary Euljiro alley of plastic tables, cheap draft beer and grilled nogari (dried pollack), anchored by Manseon Hof since 1980.
description: Around Euljiro 3-ga's printing-shop lanes, hofs spill hundreds of plastic tables onto the street every evening. Crowds drink cold draft beer here with grilled nogari (dried young pollack) dipped in spicy sauce and mayo. Manseon Hof, running since 1980, started the trend and now spreads across several buildings, including rooftop sections. It is the most 'real Seoul' night out on this list: loud, cheap, very Korean, and easy for a group of 5 to grab a table. Naver reviewers rate it highly for value (394 mentions) and for group gatherings.

name: Gwaenchana Sadang-iya
summary: Hand-carved Iberico ham sliced tableside at a warm, photogenic wine bar near Sadang.
description: Tucked into a quiet street on the Seocho/Sadang border, this wine bar built its name (a playful "it's okay, Sadang" pun) on Bellota-grade Iberico ham carved by hand at the table, paired with truffle-cream gnocchi and a well-chosen glass-pour wine list. The dining room is intimate and warmly lit with a private room available — good for a small group wanting a quieter conversation over wine rather than a loud bar scene.
tips: Ask staff for a wine recommendation — reviewers say every suggestion landed well.
No on-site parking; use nearby public lots.

name: Hanchu
summary: Two-decade-old Sinsa-dong chimaek hof, famous for double-fried chicken and crispy fried chilli peppers with cold beer.
description: Hanchu is a single-location hof near Garosu-gil that has fried chicken for over 20 years; it is not a franchise. Regulars come for double-fried chicken tossed with chilli, pork-stuffed fried green peppers, and pitchers of ice-cold beer. Naver lists over 1,600 visitor reviews, most praising the food, and marks it as good for group gatherings (203 mentions). TripAdvisor opinion is split: some visitors love the crunch, while others find the chicken dry. Treat it as a lively local chimaek night, not a gastronomic event.
tips: Closed 24–26 Sep for Chuseok and every Sunday. For the family, the best nights are Mon 28–Wed 30 Sep.
Opens at 14:00, so a late-afternoon chimaek after Garosu-gil shopping beats the evening queue.
Share a couple of chicken orders among 5, plus a plate of the stuffed peppers.
9 min from Apgujeong Stn Exit 5 (Line 3, direct from home) or a short taxi from Sinsa.

reviews.text: Naver visitors overwhelmingly praise the food (811 mentions) and say it is great for group gatherings.

name: Haneum Seongsu
summary: Seongsu gastro-pub pairing Korea's traditional liquors with modern anju such as octopus bossam and beef tartare.
description: Haneum is a modern yori-jujeom a minute from Ttukseom Station, popular with Seongsu's young crowd for its menu of Korean traditional liquors. The anju (drinking food) is serious: garlic octopus bossam, sushi-style hot pots, yukhoe (beef tartare) and seafood-and-chive jeon. It has over 1,200 Naver visitor reviews, with more than a thousand praising the food and 552 the drink range. It accepts reservations and group tables, so it is a comfortable way for parents to try sool beyond soju.
tips: Closed Sat 26 Sep (Chuseok) and every Sunday. Open 24 and 25 Sep.
Pair it with an afternoon at Seoul Forest or the Seongsu pop-ups; Ttukseom Stn Exit 7 or 8 is 1–2 min away.
Ask staff for a tasting-style mix of takju (makgeolli) and yakju (clear rice wine) to share among 5.

name: Highball Garden
summary: Izakaya-style highball specialist between Sinsa and Apgujeong — a different whisky-and-soda combo poured daily.
description: A dedicated highball bar just off the Sinsa/Apgujeong border, with soft bar lighting and a terrace. The bartenders rotate "today's highball" using a different whisky paired with soda or ginger ale, plus fruitier pisco, yuzu and wasabi riffs for the more adventurous. It's a relaxed, conversational bar — closer to a Tokyo izakaya than a loud cocktail club — and a good easy introduction to whisky highballs for guests who don't want a full cocktail menu.

Pisco highball with grape, pineapple & coconut water

name: Jangsaeng Health Center
summary: A former Korean herbal-tonic shop in Yeongdong Market reborn as a nostalgic, open-year-round cocktail bar.
description: Jangsaeng ("longevity") was once literally a geongangwon — a traditional Korean herbal tonic shop — inside Yeongdong Market near Nonhyeon Station, and the new owners kept the old apothecary bones while turning it into a cocktail bar. The concept plays on that history: a "naengmyeon cocktail" and other tongue-in-cheek riffs on Korean comfort food alongside proper cocktails, served in a warmly lit room with market-worn charm. It's open every day of the year, which makes it a reliable pick even around the Chuseok holiday.
highlights: Concept cocktails riffing on Korean comfort food
Braised pork belly (dongpa-yuk style) and kimchi
tips: Open 365 days a year — a safe bet if other bars close for Chuseok.
Sits inside old Yeongdong Market — half the fun is the walk in past shuttered market stalls at night.

name: Jusindang (Zoo Sindang) Gangnam
summary: Shaman-shrine themed bar with a cocktail for each of the 12 Korean zodiac animals, 3 min from Gangnam Station.
description: Jusindang (酒神堂, 'house of the god of drink') turns Korean shamanic imagery into a moody, design-forward bar. The menu has one cocktail for each of the 12 zodiac animals (rat, ox, tiger and so on), so each family member can order their own birth-year drink. Unlike most cocktail bars, the Gangnam branch runs a proper Korean-modern kitchen: grilled hanwoo steak, sous-vide beef short rib, spicy fish stew and potato jeon. With 9,500 Naver visitor reviews, it is a Seoul favourite with locals yet little known to tourists.
highlights: Potato jeon and gondre noodles for sharing
Lunch and evening set courses from ₩18,000
tips: Look up each person's Korean zodiac animal by birth year before you go; it is a fun ritual to order by sign.
Opens 11:00 with a 15:00–17:00 break, so a lunch course here is an easy daytime taste of the concept for parents.
Naver lists reservations and a high chair for this branch. Book for 5 on weekends, when the Gangnam queue gets long.
Gangnam Stn Exit 11 (Line 2 / Shinbundang), 3 min walk. It is 2 stops from Gyodae on Line 2.

name: Kkokkio Firewood Chicken
summary: Two-floor Gangnam pub for firewood-roasted chicken, golbaengi and nogari with soju or beer; open until 03:30.
description: Kkokkio is a big, busy Gangnam Station pub built around whole chicken roasted over firewood. The house special is hanbang nurungji tongdak: herbal chicken on crispy scorched rice. Around it sit the classic Korean drinking anju: spicy golbaengi with noodles, fire-grilled boneless chicken feet, nogari and meoktae (dried pollack), and pojangmacha udon. At ₩19,900 for the signature chicken, it is solid value for Gangnam. Naver visitors praise the food (1,222 mentions) and the roomy two floors (527).

Golbaengi somyeon (spicy sea snails with noodles)

summary: A 24th-floor hotel lounge at Josun Palace with 30-foot windows, live jazz piano and a deep whisky and champagne list.

summary: Original taproom of Magpie, the Itaewon brewery that helped start Korea's craft-beer boom, pouring fresh Jeju-brewed drafts.
description: Magpie Brewing was founded in Itaewon's Gyeongnidan in 2012 by four beer-loving friends and helped spark Korea's craft-beer revolution. The Brewshop keeps the original concept: just great beer, with fresh drafts shipped from Magpie's brewery on Jeju. There is no kitchen, but you can bring food or order delivery. It is small and casual, rated 4.5 on TripAdvisor, and good value for a beer-lover's hour before dinner in Itaewon or Haebangchon.
highlights: Magpie Pale Ale, Porter and IPA on draft

name: M+MS
summary: Café by day, experimental fermentation cocktail bar by night; new at No. 42 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026.
description: M+MS is the newcomer of the 2026 list, entering Asia's 50 Best Bars at No. 42. It runs as a café in the afternoon, then turns into a cocktail bar with its own in-house brewing and fermentation programme. The drinks are deliberately experimental; the list's write-up singles out Yama, made with sour kimchi and tuna. Naver reviewers call it the most-talked-about bar in Apgujeong right now, and it has a perfect 5.0 visitor score there.
highlights: Experimental signature drinks such as the kimchi-and-tuna Yama
Opens at 14:00, so it works as an afternoon stop
tips: The 14:00 opening makes it one of the few Asia's 50 Best bars you can visit in daylight, which suits parents who prefer an early evening.
No valet parking: use the public lot on Dosan-daero 45-gil. It is 7 min from Apgujeong Rodeo Stn Exit 5.
Closed on Chuseok day (25 Sep).

reviews.text: Korea Herald notes it works as a café in the afternoon and a cocktail bar in the evening, with an in-house brewery and fermentation programme.
A Naver reviewer calls it the most-watched bar in Apgujeong right now. Very experimental cocktails with a different feel from the other ranked bars.

name: MOBO Bar (JW Marriott Hotel Seoul)
subcategory: Hotel botanical cocktail bar with garden terrace
summary: A 'modern botanical' cocktail bar on JW Marriott Banpo's 7th floor, with its own greenhouse and garden terrace, two Line 3 stops from home.
description: MOBO (short for 'modern botanical') is on the 7th floor of JW Marriott Hotel Seoul, above Express Bus Terminal and the Shinsegae Gangnam complex. A long dark-wood bar faces a wall of grow-lit shelves. Behind it are a glass greenhouse where the team grows herbs and fruit for the drinks, and an open-air garden terrace with sofas. The cocktail list is built around five themes (Tonic, Fruits, Herbs, Spices and Earth). In 2025 Forbes Travel Guide put it on its 58 Star Bars list, the only bar in Korea to make it. It is TripAdvisor's top-rated hotel bar in this group and the closest to home.
highlights: Garden terrace on a mild late-September evening
Herb-forward signature cocktails such as Herb of Grace (₩29,000) and San Martini (₩38,000)
Forbes Travel Guide 2025 Star Bar (only one in Korea)
tips: The easiest nightcap from home: two stops on Line 3 to Express Bus Terminal, or a short taxi. It stays open until 02:00 on Friday and Saturday.
Ask for the outdoor terrace sofas for 5. Naver reviewers single out the outdoor space (야외공간이 멋져요), and the terrace suits parents better than bar stools.
Marriott's listing marks it as not taking reservations, so arrive early on Friday and Saturday or phone +82-2-6282-6739 to check.
Hotel parking at JW Marriott is free for 5 hours, per Naver.

reviews.text: Cozy bar with good food & drinks and, above all, great service.
reviews.author: Peter

reviews.text: The atmosphere is very good and the cocktails are fresh and delicious.
Korean visitors praise the outdoor terrace atmosphere, the bartenders' skill and the service, while noting that prices are hotel-level.
On Naver, visitors most often vote for tasty food, kind staff, a wide drinks list, the interior and the outdoor space.

name: Monday Blues
summary: Seocho-side wine bistro near Gangnam Station: 72-hour pork belly, sirloin steak and paella with a friendly wine list.
description: Monday Blues is a wine bar and bistro on the Seocho side of Gangnam Station, in the lobby of the Samsung Chervill building. It is serious about food: 72-hour slow-cooked pork belly, sirloin steak, crab rosé pasta and squid-ink paella, all built for sharing with a bottle. Naver visitors praise the food first (646 mentions) and the interior second, with 1,155 blog reviews. It opens at 11:00 for lunch, which makes an early family dinner easy, and it is about 15 minutes from home.
tips: Holiday schedule on Naver: open 24 and 26 Sep (11:00–23:00 with a 15:00–17:00 break), closed on Chuseok day (25 Sep).
Gangnam Stn Exit 5 (Shinbundang) is 2 min away. Turn right at the Samsung Fire alley; it is in the building lobby by Kkanbu Chicken.
Book a table for 5 on Naver; it is group-friendly and has parking.

reviews.text: Naver visitors praise the food above all (646 mentions), then the interior and a room that is good for talking.
Reviewers highlight distinctive dishes and friendly staff.

name: Mood Seoul (Some Sevit)
summary: Wine bar on Some Sevit's floating Solbit island, near home, with Han River night views by Banpo Bridge.
description: Mood Seoul occupies Solbit, one of the Some Sevit floating islands on the Han River beside Banpo Bridge. It is the closest real riverside night-view bar to home. The wine list comes with a full kitchen; the signature is pomodoro pasta topped with lobster, snow crab, octopus, abalone and shrimp. Naver visitors rate the interior highest (377 mentions), then the food. With the water all around and the city lit up across the river, it is a comfortable, parent-friendly way to do 'Seoul at night'.
highlights: Han River and Banpo Bridge views from a floating island
Wine by the glass and bottle
tips: Closed Thu 24 Sep for Chuseok; open 25 and 26 Sep. Weekday kitchen closes early (last order 20:30), so book 18:00–19:00.
Getting there: Express Bus Terminal Stn Exit 4 then bus 740 one stop, or a 20-min walk from Exit 8-1. A taxi from home is quickest.
Walk the Banpo Hangang Park riverside afterwards; the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain is on Banpo Bridge right next door (check the day's show times).

reviews.text: Naver visitors rate the interior and setting highest, followed by the food and friendly service.
The seafood pomodoro pasta with lobster and snow crab is the dish most visitors order.

price.note: Wine and dining; seafood pasta is the signature

name: Olivier by Syoten
summary: Apgujeong Rodeo izakaya-wine bar built around sashimi platters, mackerel-potato maki and natural wine.
description: A sleek, European-toned seafood izakaya just off Apgujeong Rodeo, pairing fresh sashimi platters, grilled lamb chops and a famous mackerel-and-potato maki with a well-curated wine list. It reads more like a stylish wine-and-seafood dining room than a loud bar, which makes it an easy pick for parents who want good food alongside their glass of wine. Reviewers consistently single out the food quality as much as the atmosphere.
highlights: Mackerel & potato maki — the house signature
Grilled lamb chops with black garlic sauce
tips: Corkage fee applies if bringing your own bottle.
No parking on-site — use nearby public lots.
A 5-min walk from Apgujeong Rodeo Station Exit 5.

Diners rave that "everything on the menu is delicious," recommending the lamb chops and abalone-intestine pasta alongside a good bottle of wine.

name: The Paris Bar (Grand Hyatt Seoul)
summary: Grand Hyatt's French-styled bar on Namsan, with live jazz, signature cocktails and Seoul city lights beyond the windows.
description: The Paris Bar sits below the lobby of the Grand Hyatt Seoul, high on the slope of Namsan. The hotel describes live jazz performances with the city lights of Seoul visible indoors or out. The room is discreet and stylish with French touches, and pairs signature cocktails with French-inspired snacks. For parents it is the most classic, comfortable way to enjoy a night view: armchairs, valet parking and five-star service.
highlights: Live jazz sets in the evening
City-light views from the Namsan hillside
Signature cocktails and French-inspired bar snacks

Reserve a window table on TableCheck.

name: Pine & Co
summary: A creative speakeasy down an Apgujeong back alley, ranked among Asia's 50 Best Bars, known for its kimchi cocktail.
description: Pine & Co is a basement speakeasy tucked down a quiet Apgujeong alley, ranked No. 50 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2024 for its playful, ingredient-driven cocktails. Signature drinks lean into Korean pantry staples — a kimchi cocktail and one featuring edible ants have both become talking points — served in a stylish, intimate underground room. It's a quieter, conversation-friendly speakeasy rather than a loud late-night scene, which suits an adult crowd looking for a well-made drink. Reservations are recommended given the small footprint.
tips: Reserve ahead — it's a small underground room near Apgujeong Rodeo.
5-minute walk from Apgujeong Rodeo Station Exit 5.
Go early evening for a calmer, more conversational atmosphere.

reviews.text: Asia's 50 Best Bars ranked Pine & Co No. 50 in 2024, citing its creative, ingredient-driven cocktail menu.

summary: Indoor-outdoor rooftop bar atop the Mondrian Itaewon, with city views, DJs, single malts and wines by the glass.
description: Privilege sits on the roof of the Mondrian Seoul Itaewon, combining a terrace with a classically styled lounge. It has one of the city's better single-malt selections and a wide list of wines by the glass, and world-class DJs set the soundtrack as the evening goes on. TripAdvisor reviewers highlight the view, the service and the cocktails. It opens at 18:00, so arrive at opening to catch dusk over the city.
highlights: DJ sets later in the evening
tips: Open 18:00–24:00, and until 02:00 on Fri and Sat. Arrive at 18:00 for sunset (about 18:30 in late September).
Reserve on CatchTable for a terrace table. Weekend nights get loud once the DJ starts, so weekdays suit parents better.
A 16-min walk from Noksapyeong Stn Exit 3; a taxi from home is simpler.

summary: Dimly lit Euljiro LP bar with shelves of vinyl, wine and whisky; request a record from the jazz-heavy collection.
description: Pyeonggyunyul is a dim second-floor LP bar right by Euljiro 3-ga Station. Walls of vinyl surround the room, and staff spin jazz and classics, taking song requests (Chet Baker is a house favourite). Guests come for wine and whisky rather than cocktails, and for the romance of the room. Naver visitors rate the music first (185 mentions), then the interior; its 893 blog reviews make it one of the best-known LP bars among young Koreans.
highlights: Wine and whisky by the glass
tips: Naver lists it as a no-kids zone, so it is adults only. The room is intimate, so a group of 5 should book.
Opens 13:00 on Saturdays (break 17:00–18:00) and 14:00 on Sundays, making it a great rainy-afternoon stop.

name: Rooftop KLOUD
summary: A 1920s-speakeasy-styled rooftop bar on the 21st floor of AC Hotel Gangnam with 360-degree views to N Seoul Tower.
description: Rooftop KLOUD sits on the 21st floor of AC Hotel by Marriott Seoul Gangnam, directly by Yeoksam Station, blending a prohibition-era speakeasy interior with an open-air terrace that looks out to N Seoul Tower and the Gangnam skyline. It has been ranked among the world's best rooftop bars by international guides, and the crowd skews toward relaxed cocktail sipping rather than a loud club scene. Drinks run pricier than average, but reviewers say the views and attentive bartenders justify it. It's an easy after-dinner stop since it's right by a Line 2 station.
highlights: 360-degree skyline and N Seoul Tower views
Indoor speakeasy lounge plus open terrace
tips: Go right at sunset for the best light before the city lights come on.
Directly above Yeoksam Station — easy to combine with a Gangnam dinner.

name: Saeseoul
summary: Pink building with a retro arcade downstairs, a Korean-twist cocktail bar and a rooftop over the Jongno 3-ga hanok roofs.
description: Saeseoul stacks a retro game arcade on the lower floors, a cocktail bar on the third and a rooftop terrace looking over the low hanok roofs of Ikseon-dong and Jongno. Cocktails come with alcohol, sweetness and acidity ratings on the menu, and several are named after arcade games, such as Pac-Man. It sits right at the mouth of the Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha street, where orange-tented street stalls set up every evening. With over 5,600 Naver visitor reviews, it is hugely popular with young Seoulites but rarely on tourist lists.
highlights: Rooftop views over Ikseon-dong hanok roofs
Retro arcade games on the way up
Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha tent street right outside
tips: Naver lists it as a no-kids zone, which is fine for adults. Book the rooftop for groups on Naver.
Blankets are provided on cool evenings, and late-September nights can be chilly up top.
Combine it with the orange-tent pojangmacha stalls on the street outside for an easy two-stop night.
Jongno 3-ga Stn Exit 4 is 2 min away. Closed on Chuseok day (25 Sep).

reviews.text: Over 2,700 Naver visitors single out the view, alongside the drink range and good food.

summary: Two-floor dining pub near Gyodae with a huge sound system, draught Guinness, whisky highballs and hearty plates.
description: Saloon 4350 bills itself as a luxury dining pub with an 'overwhelming' speaker system, and music is part of the draw: Naver reviewers single out the sound (185 mentions). It spreads over two floors on Seocho-daero 46-gil, 3 min from Gyodae, so a group of 5 can sprawl. The menu covers draught Guinness and Stella, craft pale ale, highballs from Kakubin to Hakushu, bottles of wine and single malts. The food is substantial: Chicago-style pizza, a sirloin steak with ghee butter, gambas and golbaengi.

The kitchen covers wine-friendly plates such as lamb-rack steak, abalone cream risotto, gambas, charcuterie and pizzas. Charcuterie and cheese platters with bottle wine

summary: Yeouido's iconic 63 Building observatory, reopened June 2026 with a rooftop deck, art space and Starbucks 60 floors above the Han River.

description: Songdo Central Park runs a 1.8 km seawater canal (with boats on it) through Incheon's planned international business district, built on reclaimed mud flats. name: Suwon Hwaseong
summary: A complete 18th-century city wall, 5.5 km of it, with a restored palace inside — the easiest day trip on the list by train.
description: Suwon Hwaseong is a complete UNESCO-listed fortress wall from 1796, 5.5 km around, with a town that still lives inside the gates and a restored royal palace, Hwaseong Haenggung, in the middle. Walking the full loop means a climb over Paldalsan; the flat northern stretch from Janganmun to Hwaseomun is the good part for a family that wants the view without the hill. The wall itself is free and open 24 hours; only the palace charges admission. Line 1 runs directly to Suwon Station from central Seoul, making this the simplest day trip out of the eight covered here, but budget most of a day including local transfer from the station to the wall — it is well outside the subway network the family uses at home.

description: Shinsegae Food Market is the department-store chain's stand-alone gourmet-supermarket format, and the Dogok branch is a bright, well laid-out example just one subway stop from Seocho — imported and Korean groceries, a curated wine section, bakery, and several counter restaurants (a popular conveyor-belt sushi spot among them) sharing the same floor. It's a genuinely relaxing, air-conditioned browse for grocery-loving parents, and doubles as a practical stop for snacks, banchan, or a quick meal without committing to a full restaurant sit-down. Free parking makes it easy if renting a car for part of the trip.
highlights: Imported groceries, wine cellar, bakery and deli counters under one roof
In-store conveyor-belt sushi and other quick-eat counters
2 minutes from Dogok Station Exit 4 — one stop from Seocho on Line 3
tips: Good spot to grab pre-made banchan, fruit or a light meal without a restaurant reservation
The sushi-go-round counter (Gatten Sushi) inside gets a line at lunch — go before noon or after 1:30pm
Free parking makes it an easy detour if you have a rental car
A relaxed rainy-day browse for the whole group, not just a quick grocery run

reviews.text: Satisfying overall — good selection and free parking made it an easy stop.
With over 600 Google reviews, it's a solid neighborhood option for imported groceries and a quick counter meal.
A visitor recommended the in-store Gatten Sushi conveyor-belt counter as a reliable, no-queue-hassle lunch option most times of day.

name: Shinsegae Department Store Gangnam
summary: Korea's top-grossing department store, right above Express Bus Terminal: Sweet Park dessert hall, House of Shinsegae dining, luxury floors.
description: Shinsegae Gangnam sits on top of Express Bus Terminal station, one stop from home on Line 3, and is the store Seoulites treat as the benchmark. Its renovated food floors are the draw: Sweet Park (opened Feb 2024) packs 43 dessert brands into about 5,300 m² of Grand Central-style arcades, House of Shinsegae (June 2024) is a dim, hotel-like dining and wine hall open until 22:00, and Shinsegae Market sells premium produce and gifts. Above them are every major luxury house, Korean designers and a big beauty floor. Easy to pop into repeatedly during the week.
highlights: Sweet Park — Korea's largest dessert hall (43 brands incl. Pierre Marcolini, Mille & Un, Fortnum & Mason)
House of Shinsegae — low-lit restaurant hall and ~5,000-bottle Wine Cellar, open to 22:00

Full luxury and K-beauty floors under one roof

CLOSED Thu 24 and Fri 25 Sep; open Sat 26 onward (extended hours to 20:30 Fri–Sun).
House of Shinsegae restaurants stay open to 22:00 (last order 1 h before) — good for a late family dinner after the store closes.
Spend ₩50,000+ for 1 h free parking; foreign shoppers get tax refunds on eligible purchases (bring passports).

name: Shinsegae Department Store Main Store & The Heritage
summary: Korea's first department store (1930s building) plus The Heritage, a restored 1935 bank with Korean craft floor and a giant media facade.
description: Shinsegae's flagship faces the Bank of Korea roundabout between Myeongdong and Namdaemun Market: an early-20th-century main building joined to a modern wing. Across the lane, The Heritage (opened 9 April 2025) restores a 1935 bank — Seoul cultural heritage — with a Peter Marino-designed Chanel on 1–2F, a 4F museum of Myeongdong's retail history and House of Shinsegae Heritage on 5F showcasing Korean crafts with a dessert salon. After dark the store's wraparound digital media facade lights the whole square. The basement food hall is a long-time office-lunch favourite.

Shinsegae Square media facade on the main building after dark

Line 4 Hoehyeon Station Exit 7 leads straight in; pair with Namdaemun Market (next door) or Myeongdong (5 min walk) — but Namdaemun is shut 24–27 Sep.
Come just after sunset to see the media facade, then eat in the food hall.

The basement food hall is one of the city's biggest, and the 5th-floor Sounds Forest indoor garden is the place to sit down. It is the most 'future Seoul' of the city's department stores and an easy half-day with parents.

name: Dialogue in the Dark Bukchon
subcategory: Sensory experience (guided tour in total darkness)
summary: A 100-minute guided walk through pitch-black rooms led by a blind guide — the globally franchised sensory-empathy exhibit, in Bukchon.
description: Dialogue in the Dark is an internationally franchised experience (running in dozens of cities since the 1980s) where small groups are led entirely by touch, sound and smell through simulated everyday spaces — a park, a market, a boat — by a visually-impaired guide, with zero light the whole way. It's seated/walking only, no climbing or exertion, and genuinely popular with adults: reviewers describe it as calming and perspective-shifting rather than a haunted-house scare. Sessions run every 15 minutes and last about 100 minutes, so it fills a relaxed midday slot in the Bukchon/Anguk area.

name: NANTA Myeongdong Theatre
summary: Wordless percussion-comedy show — four "chefs" turn kitchen tools into drums while racing to finish a wedding banquet.

It's an easy 60–90 minute evening slotted around Myeongdong street food and shopping.

summary: A spotless, 5.0-rated foot-and-body massage chain in Cheongdam — reservation-only, open 10am-midnight every day of the year.
description: The Hanoi Foot & Body is a fast-growing Vietnamese-style massage chain, and its Cheongdam Le Ciel branch (in the basement of an upscale apartment retail arcade) is one of its top-reviewed locations, with a perfect 5.0 score across 148 reviews. name: Spa Lei (women only)
summary: Women-only 24h bathhouse by Sinsa Station: seawater and open-air baths, a pine-fired bulhanjeungmak and famous body scrubs.
description: Spa Lei is a women-only sauna and jjimjilbang in Jamwon-dong, a few minutes' walk from Sinsa Station and one stop from home on Line 3. The spa styles itself on Eastern European bathhouses, with dark wood, framed photographs and a small open-air bath on a terrace, alongside a West Coast seawater bath, green-tea bath and a cold plunge that regulars rave about. The traditional bulhanjeungmak (fire-heated dome sauna) is lit with Gangwon pine at 5 am and opens at 10 am; there are also red-clay, charcoal and salt rooms. Seshin (Korean body scrub), oil massage, facials and nails are sold in-house, which is what most foreign reviewers come for.
highlights: Seshin body scrub, with oil or aroma add-ons
tips: Women only: the men in the family need somewhere else, such as the JW Marriott Seoul sauna nearby at Express Bus Terminal.
Entry is ₩22,000 for 8 hours, then ₩2,000 an hour. Several September 2026 Naver reviewers were surprised by the overtime charge, so note your entry time.
Spa Lei went viral on Instagram in September 2026 and Naver reviewers report packed weekends and Chuseok-season crowds. Go on a weekday morning, or just after 10:00 when the fire sauna opens.
Book scrubs and massages at the desk as soon as you arrive, because slots fill on busy days. Staff speak some English, according to TripAdvisor reviewers.

reviews.text: A reviewer booked the full-body scrub and oil cleanse and called it an incredible experience, even if lying on the plastic table felt comical.
A reviewer suggests spending the whole day there. The scrub and massage cost extra but are worth it.
A regular praised the variety of baths and the 'delicious' ice-cold plunge, and liked the fire sauna. They wished pool-cleaning times were posted, because they arrived at dawn and could not bathe.
Some September 2026 reviews call it packed after going viral on Instagram, with queues at the snack bar and a full fire-sauna dome. They say to go off-peak.
