name: SPAREX Dongmyo
summary: A modern 24h jjimjilbang on the 13th floor above Dongmyo Station, with a fire-kiln sauna, hinoki bath and city views, for ₩14,000.
description: SPAREX Dongmyo is a newer branch of the SPAREX chain, opened around 2024 on the 13th floor of the building beside Dongmyo Station. It replaces the big old-school bathhouses that closed after COVID, including Dragon Hill Spa and Siloam Sauna. It is bright and modern, with gender-separated baths and dry and wet saunas, then a shared hall in spa clothes with a bulhanjeungmak (fire-heated dome), hwangto clay, salt, ice and hinoki rooms. There is also a food court serving sikhye, roasted eggs and Korean set meals, a well-equipped gym and screen golf. Locals love it: 7,700+ Naver reviews single out how clean it is, its size and its fair price.
highlights: Bulhanjeungmak fire domes and a hinoki forest-bath room
Food court: sikhye, roasted eggs, jeyuk and miyeok-guk
tips: Hidden gem: over 7,700 Naver visitor reviews but only a handful on TripAdvisor. Go straight out of Dongmyo Station Exit 6 and up to the 13th floor.
Entry is ₩14,000 from 05:00–20:00 or ₩16,000 from 20:00–05:00, valid for 24 hours. Parking is free for 3 hours (official Instagram, June 2026).
Bring your own shampoo and a few ₩1,000 notes or coins, because hairdryers are coin-operated. Baths close for cleaning late at night (women's roughly 23:00–01:00, men's 00:00–02:00).
Pair it with the Dongmyo flea market or Dongdaemun (one stop on Line 1 or 6). It is also a cheap, rainy-evening reset for a group of 5.

reviews.text: A September 2026 reviewer found everything clean because it is fairly new. They liked the high-floor views, the jeyuk and seaweed-soup dinner and the reasonable price, and plan to return.
Another reviewer found the scrub short and the food-court tteokbokki and ramyeon undercooked. They called the food the weak spot.
A traveller said their scrub was excellent and very thorough, and that they 'felt like a new woman'.
A first-timer said nobody explained how the spa worked. Know the routine (shoe locker, bath, spa clothes) before you go.

price.note: ₩14,000 for entry 05:00–20:00 or ₩16,000 for 20:00–05:00, each valid 24 h. Scrubs and meals are extra.

hours.note: Open 24 hours, all year. Bath cleaning: women's about 23:00–01:00, men's about 00:00–02:00. No scrubs 01:00–03:00. No unaccompanied minors 22:00–05:00.

chuseok.note: Open 24/7 all year, and Naver reviews show it operating through mid-September 2026. No specific 2026 Chuseok notice was found. Holiday afternoons will be busy.

name: Supsok Hanbang Land
summary: A charcoal-kiln bathhouse on a wooded hill above Sinchon, where you roast sweet potatoes on the embers and rest on forest decks.
description: Supsok Hanbang Land (the 'forest herbal land') is one of the few Seoul jjimjilbangs that still fires real charcoal kilns (sutgama). There are low, medium and high-heat chambers, plus a hearth room where glowing charcoal sits in a brazier. It sits against Ansan's woods near Bongwonsa Temple, so between sweats you can cool off on shaded wooden decks outside. The snack bar sells sikhye and roasted eggs, and you can grill sweet potatoes, potatoes and rice cakes yourself; a separate restaurant grills samgyeopsal. Korean TV has featured it many times, and it is the most characterful of the classic big bathhouses left after Dragon Hill Spa and Siloam closed.
highlights: Charcoal kilns in three heat levels
Grill your own sweet potatoes and garaetteok (rice cakes)
tips: Bring socks, or buy them for ₩3,000: you need socks and a towel underfoot in the hottest kiln.
Adult bath plus sauna was ₩17,000 in July 2026, per a Naver review. Hairdryers are coin-operated and the coin noraebang takes cash only.
It is uphill from Sinchon and Ewha, so take a taxi from Ewha Womans Univ. Station on Line 2, direct from Seocho, rather than walking the slope with parents.
Weekends get crowded and noisy with kids. Arrive early on a weekday; the kilns run 08:00–21:00.

reviews.text: A visitor called it another fantastic jjimjilbang, and even better after hiking nearby Ansan.
A reviewer loved roasting sweet potatoes and rice cakes, the variety of sauna rooms and the resident cat, and called it a one-of-a-kind jjimjilbang in Seoul.
Other recent reviews say the building and ice room are dated and service can be curt. Come for the kilns, not polish.

price.note: About ₩17,000 for bath plus charcoal kiln, or about ₩11,000 for bath only (Trip.com guide and a July 2026 Naver review). Snacks and grilling are extra.

name: Yaksonmyungga Hanti
summary: A branch of Korea's Yaksonmyungga body-care chain, two minutes from Hanti Station — full-body and face/body care.
description: Yaksonmyungga is a well-established Korean body-care franchise (dozens of branches nationwide) specializing in manual full-body and facial-contouring treatments rather than a sauna/jjimjilbang format. The Hanti branch keeps a 4.8 rating with reviewers repeatedly praising staff warmth and tailored pressure, and it's two minutes on foot from Hanti Station, one stop from the Gangnam/Seocho area. It closes Mondays and on Chuseok Day itself, so it fits neatly around the rest of this trip window.
highlights: Full-body "Slim Body" manual massage and facial-contouring treatments
4.8-rated with reviewers highlighting attentive, tailored pressure
tips: Closed Mondays and on Chuseok Day (25 Sep) — book for another day in the window
Reserve by phone or KakaoTalk channel ahead of time
Officially listed full-body "Slim Body" care is ₩190,000; ask about shorter back-only options for a lower price
One subway stop from Seocho via Line 3/Suin-Bundang connection makes it an easy add-on to a Gangnam day

reviews.text: The deputy director was genuinely kind and gave one of the best treatments I've had.
Warm, comfortable atmosphere that helped me relax even more during the massage; would recommend to friends, including for couples.
An hour of relaxed massage in a comfortable setting was a great way to start the day, with pressure adjusted to what I needed.

price.note: Full-body "Slim Body" care ₩190,000/session (official chain price, may vary slightly by branch); back-only care from about ₩100,000.

hours.note: Closing time approximate; confirm exact last-appointment time when booking.

chuseok.note: Closed on Chuseok Day (25 Sep) only per the branch's own posted info; open 24 and 26 Sep and the rest of the trip except the regular Monday closure (28 Sep).

name: Demon Slayer: Total Concentration Exhibition
summary: Demon Slayer's first Korea exhibition in a Seongsu warehouse — closes 27 Sep, so only 26–27 Sep of this trip catch it.
description: This is the Korean debut of the "Total Concentration" (전집중) Demon Slayer touring exhibition, set up inside S-Factory's Building D in Seongsu with recreated scenes, original art panels and exclusive merchandise. It's been running since 27 June 2026 and is scheduled to close on 27 September 2026 — right in the middle of the trip window, so it's only catchable on Saturday 26 or Sunday 27 September, not the Monday/Tuesday after. Reviews are more mixed than most entries in this guide (some found the production value underwhelming for the price), so it's best treated as a fan-driven pop-in rather than a must-see, timed for anyone in the group who's into the anime.
highlights: Korea's first Demon Slayer touring exhibition, with recreated scenes and original art
Timed-entry ticketing by 15-30 min slots to manage crowds
8 minutes from Seongsu Station Exit 2, in the Seongsu warehouse-conversion district
tips: Closes 27 Sep 2026 — only Sat 26 or Sun 27 work for this trip, not the 28th or 29th
Some visitors found the exhibit thinner than expected for the ticket price — go for the merch and photo ops, not a deep dive
Book a timed slot online in advance rather than queuing on the day
Combine with a Seongsu café/shopping loop (Ttukseom/Seongsu is a short walk)

reviews.text: Went to the Demon Slayer exhibition and understood why some visitors called it disappointing — the production quality felt underwhelming for the price.
A fan who visited on a weekday said it was worth it for the calm, uncrowded viewing experience despite mixed word-of-mouth.
One visitor said it's a must for anyone who loved the Mugen Train and Infinity Castle films, primarily for the exclusive merchandise.

price.note: Weekday tickets ₩26,000; weekend tickets ₩28,000. Exhibition closes 27 Sep 2026.

hours.note: Exhibition period 27 Jun-27 Sep 2026 only; closed outside those dates regardless of the time shown.

chuseok.note: Not driven by the holiday — the exhibition simply runs 27 Jun-27 Sep 2026, so it happens to be open 26 Sep but closed by 27 Sep evening / definitely closed 28-30 Sep.

location.address: 1F, S-Factory Building D, 11 Yeonmujang 15-gil, Seongdong-gu, Seoul

name: MMCA Free Chuseok Days & Do Ho Suh Retrospective
summary: All MMCA branches free 24–27 Sep; the Seoul branch’s Do Ho Suh retrospective is 2026’s hottest show (closed 25 Sep).
description: MMCA opens its Seoul, Gwacheon, Deoksugung and Cheongju branches free of charge for Chuseok. The Seoul branch’s large Do Ho Suh retrospective — three decades of fabric architecture, thread drawings and recent projects about home and identity — draws queues daily. Also showing: Korea Artist Prize 2026 and "This Is (Not) Conceptual Art". Deoksugung branch shows Lee Dai-won inside the palace.
highlights: Do Ho Suh’s translucent fabric houses
tips: Free but ticketed — book online; if sold out, on-site timed tickets are first-come.
Seoul branch closed 25 Sep; Deoksugung and Gwacheon branches open all four days.
Instagram #2026추석맞이국현미 (23–27 Sep) enters a Do Ho Suh soap draw.

reviews.text: Kyunghyang says the Do Ho Suh show has people queuing daily and on-site slot tickets are issued first-come when online sells out.
YTN notes MMCA Seoul also shows Christine Sun Kim, Korea Artist Prize 2026 and a conceptual-art survey.

price.note: Free 24–27 Sep (ticket required)

hours.note: Seoul branch about 10:00–18:00 with late evenings on some days

chuseok.note: Free 24, 26, 27 Sep at MMCA Seoul (closed 25 Sep); other branches open all four days.

name: Pokemon Mega Festa: Pikachu's Autumn Outing
summary: A free, hanbok-themed Pikachu pop-up and stamp rally at HiKR Ground near Jonggak — running 18 Sep-11 Oct 2026, so it spans the whole trip.
description: Korea Tourism Organization's HiKR Ground cultural space hosts this free Pokemon Korea pop-up through 11 October 2026, themed around Pikachu and friends dressed in hanbok wandering through a folk-painting-style autumn scene. The shop and main photo sets sit on the 5th floor, with a stamp rally spanning the 1st-3rd floors that hands out a 30th-anniversary Pokemon sticker once two stamps are collected. It's completely free, indoors, air-conditioned, and genuinely low-effort — a good complement to a Gwanghwamun/Jongno sightseeing day.
highlights: Free Pikachu-in-hanbok photo zones and folk-painting-themed sets (5F)
Stamp rally across floors 1-3 with a free Pokemon 30th-anniversary sticker reward
Instagram-follow bonus: a free sun cap for early visitors who follow @pokemon_korea_official
tips: Runs 18 Sep-11 Oct 2026, so all four trip days (26-29 Sep) are covered
Open 10:00-20:00 daily; go on a weekday morning to avoid the opening-time queue
Combine with Gwanghwamun/Cheonggyecheon or Kyobo Book Centre, both nearby
HiKR Ground's other floors have free K-culture/VR experiences worth a look while you're there

reviews.text: A space that packages a taste of Korean culture into one accessible spot — foreigners will love it, especially the interactive song-and-dance corner.
A parent visiting with kids called the folk-painting-style photo zones the most memorable spot of their autumn outing.
Fun and varied — a good free stop in central Seoul.

price.note: Free entry to the pop-up and stamp rally; optional Pokemon Korea goods for sale in the shop.

chuseok.note: No specific Chuseok-day closure notice found for the pop-up itself; HiKR Ground is inside a government-run (Korea Tourism Organization) building, which occasionally adjusts hours on the holiday — call ahead for 25 Sep specifically. The other trip days (26-29 Sep) fall within the confirmed 18 Sep-11 Oct 2026 run.

location.address: 5F (shop) / 1F-3F (stamp rally), HiKR Ground, Korea Tourism Organization Bldg, 40 Cheonggyecheon-ro, Jung-gu, Seoul

name: Seoul Autumn Festa 2026
summary: Umbrella festival linking some 200 dance, gugak, theatre and outdoor shows across Seoul, 18 Sep – 29 Nov 2026.
description: Seoul Autumn Festa ties together hundreds of performances and festivals across the city for 73 days, opening with "Seoul, Dance on the Han River" at Ttukseom on 18 Sep. During the trip it offers dance, gugak and theatre programmes, many outdoors and free. Check the festival listings for shows on your free evenings.
highlights: Dance, gugak and theatre across the city
tips: Browse the programme for events near Banpo or Seoul Arts Center to keep evenings close to home.
The Seoul Hangang International Dance Festival follows at Banpo’s Yebit Island stage on 1–3 Oct.

reviews.text: News1 reports the Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture runs the 73-day festival from 18 Sep to 29 Nov.
Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon attended the Ttukseom opening, where the festival was described as linking pure performing-arts festivals.

price.note: Many shows free; some ticketed

hours.note: Varies by performance

chuseok.note: Festival spans the holiday; individual shows vary — check listings.

name: Seoul Outdoor Library — Chuseok Late Nights
summary: Beanbags, books and lights at Seoul Plaza, Gwanghwamun and Cheonggyecheon — open until 22:00, 25–27 Sep.
description: Seoul’s popular Outdoor Library sets out bookshelves, beanbags and parasols in three downtown spots. Over Chuseok 2026 all three — "Reading Seoul Plaza", "Gwanghwamun Book Yard" and "Reading Clear Stream" on Cheonggyecheon — run from 16:00 to 22:00. It is a relaxed, free evening stop after the palaces.
highlights: Gwanghwamun Book Yard beside the Sejong statue
tips: Free and walk-in; English picture books are limited — come for the atmosphere.
Perfect tired-family pause between Gyeongbokgung and dinner.

reviews.text: Seoul city says the three Outdoor Library sites extend to 22:00 daily from 25 to 27 Sep.
Commons photos from Oct 2025 show readers relaxing in the Cheonggyecheon outdoor library.

price.note: Free

chuseok.note: Extended 16:00–22:00 on 25–27 Sep 2026; regular schedule on other days — check the Seoul Outdoor Library site.

name: Yeouido World Night Market (Bamdokkaebi)
summary: Seasonal riverside night market at Yeouido Hangang Park's Mulbit Square — international street food trucks with Han River and skyline views.
description: The World Night Market is one of the Seoul Bamdokkaebi Night Market series, set up seasonally at Yeouido Hangang Park's Mulbit Square (물빛광장) with international street-food trucks, craft vendors and performance stages against a Han River backdrop. The Bamdokkaebi series runs roughly April through October across several Hangang parks and city sites (Yeouido, Banpo, DDP, Cheonggyecheon), typically evenings on weekends. It's an easy, no-effort way to graze a variety of food while watching the river and skyline light up.
highlights: International street-food trucks and craft vendors
Performance stages and pop-up experience zones
Combine with a walk or bike ride along Yeouido Hangang Park
tips: This is a seasonal weekend market (roughly April–October) — whether it runs during the Chuseok weekend (25–27 Sep 2026) is unconfirmed; check Visit Seoul or social media before going.
Bring cash/mobile pay — many food-truck vendors are cash- or app-only.
Combine with a sunset walk in Yeouido Hangang Park before the market opens.

reviews.text: One of several Bamdokkaebi Night Market venues across Seoul (Yeouido, Banpo, DDP, Cheonggyecheon), typically operating April–October.
Rated 4.0/5 from early visitor ratings, noting the international food-truck variety and the Han River backdrop at Mulbit Square.

price.note: Free entry; pay per item at food trucks and vendor stalls.

hours.note: Seasonal, roughly April–October, typically Friday–Sunday evenings 18:00–23:00 when running — exact 2026 September schedule not confirmed.

chuseok.note: Seasonal weekend market (~Apr–Oct), typically Fri–Sun evenings. Whether it runs during Chuseok weekend (25–27 Sep 2026) is unconfirmed — no official 2026 schedule found. Check Visit Seoul or the market's social channels before going.

name: Yoo Youngkuk: The Mountain Is Within Me
summary: Free, largest-ever retrospective of Korea’s abstract painter of mountains at SeMA Seosomun, to 25 Oct 2026.
description: Marking the 110th anniversary of his birth, the Seoul Museum of Art presents about 170 works and archives by Yoo Youngkuk — including 115 oil paintings — tracing six decades of bold colour-field mountains. Admission is free and no reservation is needed. The museum is open through Chuseok.
highlights: Archive of a Korean abstraction pioneer
tips: Fridays open to 21:00 ("Seoul Culture Night"); closed Mondays.
Five minutes from Deoksugung — pair them in one evening.

reviews.text: Kyunghyang’s Chuseok exhibition guide calls it the biggest retrospective of Yoo’s lifelong focus on mountains, free 24–27 Sep.
Listings give the run as 19 May – 25 Oct 2026, Tue–Fri 10:00–20:00 and weekends 10:00–19:00, Fridays to 21:00.

price.note: Free

hours.note: Closed Mondays; holidays 10:00–19:00.

chuseok.note: Seoul city museums open and free 24–27 Sep 2026.
